lead.label: 15d
lead.why: Abstract: '6a and 15d demonstrated potent antiproliferative effects... Based on its impressive pharmacodynamic data in vitro, we conducted a study to evaluate the efficacy of 15d in a xenograft tumor model... 15d could be promising drug candidates'; conclusion: 'The most promising lead compound, 15d'.

reactions.conditions: General procedure 4.4.2: sulfonyl chloride (1.2 eq) in THF added at -5 C to 12 and Et3N (2 eq) in THF, then r.t. 6 h; 78-89 %. (Scheme 3 caption says NaH, THF.)
HCl in ethyl acetate (4 N), r.t. (Boc removal, procedure of 4.2.2); free base written, HCl salt ignored.
HATU (1.2 eq), DIPEA (3 eq), DMF, r.t. 2 h (procedure 4.2.3, 'according to the method of 6a-6j').

notes: 4 steps. Compound 5 is stated to be 'commercially available' but its structure/name is never printed in the text; SMILES derived from the product names (2-fluoro-5-[(4-oxo-3,4-dihydrophthalazin-1-yl)methyl]benzoic acid, the olaparib acid; no doubt). Enaminone 7 is used without any stated source or preparation (not said to be purchased; treated as starting material). The acyl/sulfonyl chloride for 15d is not printed as a name; cyclopropanesulfonyl chloride inferred from 15d's name. Names of 13 and 14 not given. Conflict: Scheme 3 caption says NaH for the sulfonylation, experimental says Et3N. The sulfonyl position (N2 of the pyrazole) is taken from the printed name of 15d. 12 is printed as 'tert-butyl 2,4,6,7-tetrahydro-5H-pyrazolo[4,3-c]pyridine-5-carboxylate'.
